newsitem.title: UK: Fleming beefs up corporate finance with new hires.
newsitem.headline: Fleming beefs up corporate finance with new hires.

text.p: British independent investment bank Robert Fleming said on Sunday it had made three key appointments to its corporate finance team.
A Flemings spokesman told Reuters the firm had hired Anthony McGrath from Barings as chief operating officer to replace Peter Barton who is moving to a senior marketing role in the department.
Flemings said McGrath would be responsible for the business management of its corporate finance business "as well as maintaining a number of important client relationships".
Barton will concentrate on developing high-level relationships in Europe and would also work with the financial services group within the corporate finance arm, Flemings said.
The investment bank said it had also appointed Howard Lack, who was previously with Chase Manhattan, to head project finance for Europe, the Americas, Africa and the Middle East.
He will work in collaboration with Flemings' Asian-based energy and infrastructure group and its structured finance group.
Flemings has also hired Les Pugh as a director and head of its food and beverage industry group. Pugh was previously director of consumer products for SBC Warburg in New York.
"Flemings has had a good start to 1997 advising clients, including Clyde Petroleum and Howden, on a number of important transactions," Bernard Taylor, Flemings' head of investment banking said.

Taylor said the appointments underlined its determination to be a leading player in advisory and financing work in Britain and oether parts of the world by industry specialisation and using its "unique geographic network".
